title: Product-key retrieval of Mirror edit codes
hypothesis: Product-key indexing over factorized subject/relation keys retrieves one of 256 edit codes with fewer search operations than a flat bank, while shared-basis Mirror codes reduce edit payload bytes without increasing wrong-scope edits. A Mirror-specific claim requires beating native product-key low-rank values.

task.metric: edit retrieval recall, positive edit NRMSE, wrong-scope activation, absent-key false activation, collision rate, actual payload bytes, lookup MAC proxy, wall time

development.selection_metric: retrieval/scope/quality/bytes/compute; exact native alias seals fresh

controls: Flat bank with explicit composite keys and full edit vectors; linear nearest-key scan
Native product-key index with direct full edit vectors
Mirror product-key index with shared delta basis plus per-edit code
Native product-key index with the same low-rank basis and coefficients

storage.authority: Actual serialized complete inference payload bytes
paid_objects: full values or shared delta basis and codes

compute: flat full-key scan MACs per query
product-key subkey score MACs per query
success_gate: At noise 0 and .25, positive retrieval recall >=0.98, edit NRMSE <=0.05, wrong-scope and absent false-activation rates <=0.01; Mirror complete bytes <=60% of flat bank and product-key retrieval MAC proxy <=50% of flat scan. Mirror-specific success additionally requires strict Pareto gain over native product-key low-rank control.
failure_gate: Any quality/scope/retrieval gate miss or exact native low-rank product-key alias without strict Pareto gain; fresh remains sealed after alias.
boundaries: Synthetic edit-key retrieval, not a language model edit benchmark
Composite key uses two independently retrieved subkeys and explicit scope check
No training or key learning; fixed key vectors isolate lookup/storage mechanism
Wrong-scope queries keep the key pair but change scope; absent queries use unindexed pairs
No credit for address combinatorics without measured retrieval and correct edit behavior
